facts.statement: Gregory Paul argued in 2019 that the vertebral column includes the first neck vertebra, leaving only ten dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The anterior tail vertebrae were opisthocoelous, featuring convex anterior sides and concave back sides that formed ball-and-socket joints.
facts.quote: The anterior vertebrae of the tail were opisthocoelous, which means they were convex on their anterior sides and concave on their back sides, forming ball-and-socket joints.

facts.statement: The ischium measured only two-thirds the length of the pubis.
facts.quote: The ischium was relatively short, measuring only two-thirds the length of the pubis.

facts.statement: The forelimbs measured 1.87 meters in height, while the hindlimbs were reconstructed at 2.46 meters.
facts.quote: The forelimbs measured 1.87 m in height in the nearly complete specimen, approximately two thirds the length of the hindlimbs, which were reconstructed at 2.46 m height.

facts.statement: The hand consisted of five vertically oriented metacarpals arranged in a semicircle.
facts.quote: The manus was composed merely of the five metacarpalia, which were orientated vertically and arranged in a semicircle.

facts.statement: Finger bones and claws were completely absent in Opisthocoelicaudia, unlike most other titanosaurs where they were present but reduced.
facts.quote: Finger bones and claws were also completely absent – in most other titanosaurs, these bones were still present though extremely reduced in size.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula of Opisthocoelicaudia is 2-2-2-1-0.
facts.quote: The phalangeal formula, which states the number of phalanges (digit bones) beginning with the innermost digit, is 2-2-2-1-0.

facts.statement: The first digit claw was roughly equal in size to the second digit claw, unlike other sauropods where it was larger.
facts.quote: The claw of the first digit was not larger than that of the second digit, as in other sauropods, but roughly equal in size.

facts.statement: Osteoderms have been found in at least ten titanosaur genera.
facts.quote: Osteoderms (bony plates formed in the skin) have been found with at least 10 titanosaur genera.

facts.statement: The discovery of osteoderms in the related Alamosaurus suggests that Opisthocoelicaudia may have also possessed them.
facts.quote: However, the closely related Alamosaurus was found to have osteoderms nearly a century after its discovery, in addition to several other closely related titanosaurs, thus raising the possibility that Opisthocoelicaudia had them as well.

facts.statement: Opisthocoelicaudia was originally classified within the family Camarasauridae alongside Camarasaurus and Euhelopus.
facts.quote: Originally, Opisthocoelicaudia was classified as a member of the family Camarasauridae, together with Camarasaurus and Euhelopus.

facts.statement: Leonardo Salgado and Rodolfo Coria classified Opisthocoelicaudia as a titanosaur within the family Titanosauridae in 1993.
facts.quote: In 1993, Leonardo Salgado and Rodolfo Coria showed Opisthocoelicaudia to represent a titanosaur and classified it within the family Titanosauridae.

facts.statement: Opisthocoelicaudia is closely related to Alamosaurus, Neuquensaurus, Rocasaurus, and Saltasaurus, forming the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Within the Lithostrotia, Opisthocoelicaudia has been found to be closely related to the genera Alamosaurus, Neuquensaurus, Rocasaurus and Saltasaurus, together forming the family Saltasauridae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Opisthocoelicaudia and Alamosaurus form a monophyletic group called Opisthocoelicaudiinae or if that group is paraphyletic.
facts.quote: Many scientists considered Opisthocoelicaudia to be most closely related to Alamosaurus, with both genera forming a monophyletic group, the Opisthocoelicaudiinae. Other scientists concluded that the Opisthocoelicaudiinae is paraphyletic (not forming a natural group).

facts.statement: Upchurch and colleagues argued in 2004 that Alamosaurus is not related to Opisthocoelicaudia and should be placed outside the Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Contradicting most other studies, Upchurch and colleagues in 2004 argued that Alamosaurus has to be placed outside the Saltasauridae as a close relative of Pellegrinisaurus, and therefore is not related to Opisthocoelicaudia at all.

facts.statement: Opisthocoelicaudia was discovered during a 1965 joint Polish-Mongolian expedition.
facts.quote: Both Opisthocoelicaudia and Nemegtosaurus were discovered during the 1965 joint Polish-Mongolian expedition.

facts.statement: In 1977, Borsuk-Białynicka classified Opisthocoelicaudia as a separate genus from Nemegtosaurus based on differences in their presumed family groups.
facts.quote: In 1977, Borsuk-Białynicka deemed Opisthocoelicaudia and Nemegtosaurus to represent separate genera because Nemegtosaurus was at this time considered to be a member of the Dicraeosauridae, while Opisthocoelicaudia seemed to be a representative of a different group, the Camarasauridae.

facts.statement: Opisthocoelicaudia is currently classified within the superfamily Titanosauria.
facts.quote: Currently, both Opisthocoelicaudia and Nemegtosaurus are classified within the Titanosauria

facts.statement: In 2005, Jeffrey Wilson suggested that Opisthocoelicaudia might be a synonym of Nemegtosaurus.
facts.quote: Jeffrey Wilson stated in 2005 that synonymy cannot be ruled out.

facts.statement: Currie and colleagues argued in 2003 and 2017 that Opisthocoelicaudia and Nemegtosaurus are likely synonyms based on new fossil evidence.
facts.quote: Currie and colleagues, in 2003 and 2017, argued that a synonymy is very probable in the light of new fossil discoveries in the Nemegt Formation.

facts.statement: In 2019, Averianov and Lopatin argued that Opisthocoelicaudia and Nemegtosaurus are distinct genera based on differences in vertebrae and femora found in 1949.
facts.quote: In 2019, Alexander O. Averianov and Alexey V. Lopatin reported Nemegt sauropod vertebrae discovered in 1949 and some femora that differed from the same bones of Opisthocoelicaudia, and stated they probably belonged to Nemegtosaurus, thereby supporting that the two genera were distinct.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest Opisthocoelicaudia carried its neck relatively straight and horizontally, contrary to earlier S-curved reconstructions.
facts.quote: Although an S-curved, swan-like ascending neck was envisaged in several subsequent reconstructions following similar depictions of better known sauropods, recent studies argue that sauropod necks were relatively straight and were carried more horizontally.

facts.statement: A 2007 study by Schwarz and colleagues proposed that Opisthocoelicaudia's back dipped towards the rear.
facts.quote: In a 2007 study, Daniela Schwarz and colleagues suggested that the back dipped towards the rear.

facts.statement: Opisthocoelicaudia may have been capable of rearing up on its hind legs to use its tail as a third leg for foraging.
facts.quote: Opisthocoelicaudia may have been able to rear up on its hindlimbs for foraging, using its tail as a third leg.

facts.statement: In 2011, Heinrich Mallison hypothesized that Opisthocoelicaudia could angle its tail to create a midsection buckle during rearing.
facts.quote: Heinrich Mallison in 2011 argued that Opisthocoelicaudia may have been able to angle the anterior part of the tail against the posterior part, producing a buckle in midsection.

facts.statement: The best-preserved Opisthocoelicaudia footprint measures 63 cm across, suggesting it was made by an individual larger than the known type specimen.
facts.quote: The best-preserved footprint measures 63 cm across, so it was probably created by an individual larger than the type specimen.

facts.statement: A preserved skin impression above a toe print shows non-overlapping scales with an average diameter of 14 mm.
facts.quote: Even a skin impression has been preserved above the impression of the first toe, which shows the non-overlapping scales, each with an average diameter of 14 mm.

facts.statement: In 2017, Nakajima and colleagues described a kidney-shaped sauropod forefoot impression, the first of its kind found in the Nemegt Formation.
